items.title: Raise the twin-stick controls closer to the action
items.what: On the main fight screens, both joysticks sit very low with a large dead band of dark floor between the arena and the controls. In the portrait gameplay shots, the fighters end around mid-screen while the sticks start near the bottom quarter, leaving roughly a full control-panel height of empty space between them.
items.why: On a phone, this visually disconnects input from outcome and makes the playfield feel split in two. It also pushes the thumbs farther from the center of the display where players are watching the fighters, increasing eye travel and making the game feel less immediate in the first seconds of play.
items.how: Move the entire control deck upward by about 60–100 px on the 390x844 baseline, or extend the move legend panel downward so it visually bridges into the sticks. Keep bottom-safe-area padding, but reduce the unused gap so the controls feel anchored to the bout.

items.title: Stop the pre-fight card and button from covering the matchup
items.what: On the 'QUALIFIER vs HasanAbi' screen, the big gold FIGHT button and countdown sit directly over the fighters’ legs and the center of the tatami, while the black tagline pill cuts across chest level. The result is that three stacked overlays occupy most of the center of the screen at once.
items.why: This is the player's first clear look at the match, and the UI blocks the exact characters and stance silhouettes they came to see. It weakens character presentation and makes the screen feel cramped before the fight even begins.
items.how: Compress the intro layout: move the tagline pill higher under the opponent name, shrink its height, and drop the FIGHT button lower so it sits just above the control area rather than over the fighters. If needed, scale the fighters up slightly and reserve the middle third of the screen for the matchup only.

items.title: Increase readability of names and round info in the top HUD
items.what: In the gameplay and intro screens, 'ASMONGOLD', 'HASANABI', and the 'ROUND 1/5 • QUALIFIER' chip are rendered very small and thin against a dark brown bar. The names especially are tiny at the far left and right edges, with wide letter spacing that reduces legibility.
items.why: These are key orientation labels players need immediately, especially on a phone held at arm’s length. If names and round state are hard to parse, the HUD feels decorative instead of informative.
items.how: Increase the player name size and weight by one step, tighten tracking, and give the round chip slightly larger text or a stronger contrast treatment. On the 390 px baseline, prioritize fewer characters per line if necessary rather than keeping the current small caps size.

items.title: Reduce the visible glow/fringe around fighter cutouts
items.what: Around both fighters, especially the white gi against the darker dojo, there is a noticeable soft halo/edge fringe. It is most obvious on outer sleeves, pant legs, and hair outlines in the gameplay screens, where the photoreal sprites look slightly pasted over the 3D scene.
items.why: This breaks the illusion of the fighters belonging in the dojo and makes the core combat presentation feel cheaper. Because the whole game revolves around looking at these two characters, compositing artifacts have outsized impact.
items.how: Tighten the sprite alpha edges and reduce any bloom contribution from the character layer. Add a subtle contact shadow or edge-darkening pass around the feet and lower body so the fighters sit into the floor instead of glowing off it.

items.title: Use the result screen’s empty middle space more effectively
items.what: On the 'HASANABI WINS' screen, the title is very high, the REMATCH button is very low, and there is a large empty vertical span in the middle with the fighters appearing small and low-contrast. The score line and the 'BOUTS WON 0/1 • BEST —' pill also feel sparse for the amount of space available.
items.why: A result screen should deliver closure and excitement, but this one feels under-filled and distant. It wastes a chance to celebrate the finish, explain progress, and drive the rematch tap.
items.how: Scale the fighters and win-state vignette up, move the score/progress block closer to them, and place the rematch CTA directly beneath the action instead of near the bottom edge. Use the middle third for a tighter victory composition rather than leaving it as mostly empty background.
